status: GROUNDWORK - DESK RESEARCH ONLY, NOTHING COLLECTED OR PUBLISHED
decided: 2026-11-02, Rohit: expand to major world cities as a sample in a future release; research first
rules: Desk-only until each city has a ground-truth plan (a local partner or a driven/walked sample) pre-registered like Hyderabad's field day.
Open data only: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), GHSL population (global), Mapillary (CC BY-SA) where coverage exists. No Google data anywhere.
Each city is measured for its own problem. The Hyderabad driving-detour index is not assumed to be the right metric everywhere.
Boxes are approximate and are checked against the Geofabrik index and the city's administrative boundary before any run.

cities.name: Metro Manila
cities.problem: Closed or time-restricted U-turn slots on divided arterials (EDSA, C-5, Quezon Avenue) force long detours; several EDSA slots were closed for the busway in 2020.
cities.metric: driving detour index (same as Hyderabad), plus before/after for slots with dated closure advisories
cities.why: Closest analogue to Hyderabad: a direct replication test of the method.

cities.name: Dhaka
cities.problem: Median U-turns and unauthorised median cuts; pedestrians avoid overpasses that sit far from desire lines.
cities.metric: driving detour index plus a walking-crossing gap (distance between legal pedestrian crossings)
cities.why: Same driving problem as Hyderabad, plus an observed walking problem that tests the second metric.

cities.name: Nairobi
cities.problem: Pedestrian severance on high-speed highways (Thika Superhighway, Outer Ring Road): footbridges far apart or blocked, pedestrians are the largest group of road deaths.
cities.metric: walking detour to the nearest legal crossing; crossing spacing per km; footbridge accessibility
cities.why: Different use case: the cost falls on people walking, not driving.
official_sources: NTSA crash statistics and hazard mapping reports

cities.name: New York City
cities.problem: Neighbourhoods split by expressways and wide arterials; a published community severance index links severance to more collisions.
cities.metric: walking and driving detour across expressways; compare with the published Community Severance Index
cities.why: Data-rich benchmark: an independent index exists to validate against.
official_sources: NYC Open Data motor vehicle collisions

cities.name: London
cities.problem: Busy arterial roads (for example Finchley Road) act as barriers to walking; a measured toolkit exists (UCL Street Mobility).
cities.metric: walking crossing gap and detour on arterials; compare with the UCL toolkit's case study
cities.why: Methodological benchmark and a possible research partner.
official_sources: TfL road network and crossing data

cities.name: Bogotá
cities.problem: Severance from bus rapid transit corridors and arterials: crossings concentrated at stations and footbridges.
cities.metric: walking crossing gap along BRT corridors; detour to the nearest station or bridge
cities.why: Tests whether a transit corridor, not only a highway, severs a neighbourhood.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.problem: Marginal expressways along rivers (Tietê, Pinheiros) and arterials split districts; few crossings over long stretches.
cities.metric: driving and walking detour across the marginal expressways
cities.why: Large-scale linear barrier case; river plus road severance.
